After transforming sentences into embeddings, these numerical vectors are clustered by uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) and hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN) to form topics100. Within each cluster, the class- based term frequency-inverse document frequency (c-TF-IDF) score is calculated for each word in each embedding. As an offspring from the early text mining metric of TF-IDF101, c-TF-IDF operates in a similar way; but, instead of looking at the relevance of a word in a document, it looks at the relevance of a word within its cluster. Some of the most common issues with TF-IDF are that it cannot capture the semantic meaning of words and it is inefficient with high dimension datasets. c-TF-IDF is appropriate to use in our application since BERT captures the semantic meaning of each sentence and the dimensionality is reduced in the clustering process. The literature on BERTopic provides a deeper explanation of this concept. It is an important nuance of BERTopic that, while LDA models assume that each document is a random collection of un-ordered words, BERTopic only analyzes one sentence at a time and uses the correlation between sequential words to understand the context. This is the main justification for employing both approaches to arrive at our results. While other researchers focus on integrating LDA and BERTopic102 to maximize coherency103 or silhouette scores104 in generated topics, our work focuses on combining the results of both models to gain insight into the importance of a predetermined topic in each corpus. These predetermined topics are referred to as categories for the remainder of this discussion. The main objectives of the research are to (1) develop a metric that ranks categories mined from topic models and (2) apply this metric to the problem of extracting MDHD EV adoption perceptions.
